coverTitle: Why Your Coding Agent Should Render Social Assets Locally
coverSubtitle: How tinytldr separates LLM distillation from deterministic Chromium + FFmpeg rendering.
author: @ajrahim · tinytldr.com

slides.title: 1. The Calling Agent Already Has Your Context
slides.body: Claude Code, Cursor, and Windsurf already read your PRs, docs, and benchmarks. Sending text to a second SaaS LLM wastes tokens and loses nuance.
slides.takeaway: Zero duplicate LLM calls or API keys inside tinytldr.

slides.title: 2. Strict Slot Contracts Prevent Layout Drift
slides.body: Every template declares strict Zod slot schemas, character budgets, and binary-search font autofit rules before Chromium ever takes a screenshot.
slides.takeaway: Overflow, contrast, and safe-zone checks run automatically.

slides.title: 3. One Spec Exports Every Platform Format
slides.body: From the exact same JSON payload, export high-DPI PNGs, multi-page LinkedIn PDFs, or 30fps H.264 MP4 animations completely offline.
slides.takeaway: 100% SHA-256 deterministic output on every run.

closingCta: Run `npx tinytldr mcp` in Claude Code or Cursor to turn your next ship into a social pack.
